claims.text: Heating as-sintered TiB2-based components in an oxygen-containing atmosphere at 800–1000°C for several hours will form an Al2O3 surface layer.
The resulting Al2O3 layer will be thin and adherent.
Controlled oxygen partial pressure is required for the proposed thermal oxidation treatment.
The treatment produces a dense, continuous, and adherent Al2O3 layer on the component surface.
The Al2O3 scale acts as a diffusion barrier between molten aluminum and the TiB2 substrate.
The Al2O3 scale minimizes diffusion of molten aluminum into the TiB2 substrate.
Minimizing aluminum diffusion reduces chemical dissolution of the TiB2-based component during high-temperature exposure.
Minimizing aluminum diffusion reduces structural degradation of the TiB2-based component during high-temperature exposure.
Thermally oxidized TiB2-based components will have a significantly lower molten-aluminum corrosion rate than untreated TiB2-based components.
Thermally oxidized TiB2-based components will retain better integrity than untreated components during prolonged molten-aluminum exposure at plating temperatures.
Protection will persist under hot-dip aluminum-plating conditions while the oxide layer remains adherent and intact.
Severe thermal cycling may cause the protective layer to spall or degrade and thereby compromise its efficacy.
Mechanical stresses may cause the protective layer to spall or degrade and thereby compromise its efficacy.

A corrosion-rate reduction of less than 20%, a lack of statistically significant improvement, or oxide spallation producing similar or accelerated degradation relative to untreated controls would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The initial material is identified only as TiB2-based and the treatment supplies oxygen, yet the proposed treatment is said to form Al2O3 before molten-aluminum exposure. No aluminum-bearing precursor, alloy constituent, coating, or prior aluminization step is specified, so the stated intervention lacks an internal source of aluminum for the claimed mediator.
